title: WPMS/775/2021 of HARDEV SINGH Vs GURU NANK SHIKSHA SAMITI

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 775 of 2021
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for respondent no.
2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Petitioners were nominated as member of the
Managing Committee in terms of Clause 9 (ii) of
Byelaws of Sri Guru Nanak Shiksha Samiti, Rudrapur,
Udham Singh Nagar, by a resolution passed by office
bearers of Managing Committee on 19.06.2019.
However, by a subsequent resolution of Managing
Committee passed on 24.02.2020, petitioners were
replaced by another set of nominated members.
Feeling aggrieved by the resolution dated
24.02.2020 passed by Managing Committee,
petitioners approached Sub-Registrar, Firms, Societies
& Chits by making a complaint, which was referred by
the Sub-Registrar to Prescribed Authority under
Section 25 of Societies Registration Act, 1860.
Petitioners are aggrieved by the order dated 16.03.2021
passed by Prescribed Authority.
It is not in dispute that petitioners became
member of the Managing Committee under Clause
9(ii) of the byelaws of the society, for ready reference
Clause 9 (ii) is reproduced below:-

"(ii) The office bearers of the managing
committee shall be elected by the general body of the
society. The remaining 10 (ten) members shall be
nominated by the office bearers of the managing
committee."
Learned counsel for petitioners submits that as
per the byelaws, Managing Committee of the Society
shall consist of (a) President; (b) Vice President; (c)
Manager; (d) Assistant Manager; (e) Treasurer; and (f)
10 (ten) members nominated by office bearers of the
Managing Committee. Thus he submits that all the
officer bearers of Managing Committee are required to
be elected by the General Body of the Society,
however, 10 (ten) members of the Managing
Committee have to be nominated by the office bearers
of the Managing Committee. Thus, he submits that
since petitioners were not elected; but, nominated and
their complaint was against their wrongful removal by
a resolution dated 24.02.2020, therefore, the issue
raised by petitioners in their complaint cannot be
termed as 'election dispute'. Thus, he contends that
Prescribed Authority had no jurisdiction to take
decision on petitioners' complaint and to uphold the
resolution passed by Committee of Management on
24.02.2020.
This Court finds substance in the submission
made by learned counsel for petitioners.
Since petitioners did not contest any election
and they became member by nomination under Clause
9 (ii) of the byelaws, therefore, their complaint against
their removal cannot be termed as 'election dispute'.

Thus, Prescribed Authority had no jurisdiction to take
decision in the matter. It appears that Prescribed
Authority mistook nomination of petitioners as
nomination of a candidate for election used in Clause
(b) and (c) of proviso to Section 25 of Societies
Registration Act for entertaining the complaint of
petitioners.
In such view of the matter, impugned order
dated 16.03.2021 passed by Prescribed Authority is
liable to be quashed and is hereby quashed.
The writ petition is allowed and the matter is
relegated to Sub-Registrar, Firms, Societies & Chits,
Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar for deciding
the issue raised in the complaint. It shall be open to
respondents to raise all contentions before Sub
Registrar.
This Court has not entered into merits of the
case, therefore, Sub-Registrar shall decide the issue on
merits untrammelled by any observation made in this
order.
